records.name: HK.sbc7_closed_form
records.entry_name: Heterogeneous Hegselmann–Krause dynamics: counterexamples to two conjectures and a theorem of Mirtabatabaei and Bullo
records.doc: A Lean 4 development of the counterexamples of Hegarty, Ognissanti and Wedin (arXiv:2610.03229) to two conjectures and a theorem of Mirtabatabaei and Bullo on heterogeneous Hegselmann–Krause dynamics. n agents with real opinions and positive bounds r_1, ..., r_n update synchronously, x(t+1) = A(x(t)) x(t), where row i of A(y) averages uniformly over the neighbourhood N_i(y): the j with |y_i - y_j| <= r_i in the SBC model (synchronized bounded confidence) and <= r_j in the SBI model (synchronized bounded influence). Conjecture 2.2 says the proximity digraph is constant after a finite time; Conjecture 2.3 says every trajectory reaches a fixed state or is eventually pseudo-stable (the agents split into two non-empty classes, fixed at their limits or moving strictly towards them from one side); Theorem 6.4(iv) says a trajectory whose digraph is constant from some time on is eventually pseudo-stable. For the four systems of the source (SBC with seven agents and rate -1/6; SBI with seven agents and rate (1 - sqrt 5)/8; SBC with six agents; a second SBI system with seven agents) the development proves the closed form x(t) = x_inf + c lambda^t v for every t, the neighbourhood of every agent at every t (alternating with the parity of t at the middle agent of the two seven-agent alternating systems, the same at every t in the other two), convergence, and that no trajectory is ever frozen or pseudo-stable after any time towards any vector, since four agents alternate sides of their limits. Hence Conjectures 2.2 and 2.3 fail in each model, and Theorem 6.4(iv) fails in each model, both in its literal reading and in the reading that also admits a fixed state. Two smaller constant-digraph systems found in this development, five SBC agents with rate (1 - sqrt 2)/3 and six SBI agents with rate (13 - sqrt 249)/40, have one real negative mode. A five-agent SBI system of this development has a complex pair of modes: the offsets of its three moving agents follow a rational averaging map from an algebraic initial offset (the real root of a cubic), its digraph is constant, it converges, and every moving agent is strictly on both sides of its limit in every five consecutive times. So Conjecture 2.3 and Theorem 6.4(iv) fail with five agents in either model. A five-agent SBC family shows that these failures persist with positive, unequal bounds whose ratio of largest to smallest is below any 1 + epsilon. Along all four source systems the final value at constant topology (Definition 3.1) of every x(t) is the limit, and in the two constant-digraph source systems the per-step convergence factor (Definition 6.1) of every agent with nonzero offset is identically the negative rate, so it converges to no non-negative number. On the positive side, Lemma 4.2 (the equi-topology neighbourhood preserves the proximity digraph) and Lemma 4.8 (a convergent trajectory whose limit has every equi-topology distance positive eventually has the digraph of its limit, the limit as its final value at constant topology, and an equilibrium limit) are proved for arbitrary bounds; the limits of the two constant-digraph systems satisfy that hypothesis, and those of the two alternating systems violate it. For the source's two spectator systems (nine SBC agents with a spectator and two beacons; eight SBI agents with a spectator) the closed forms, the constant tables and the spectator's side are proved, and along the five-agent SBC and six-agent SBI single-mode systems too the final value at constant topology is the limit and the per-step factor is the rate. Not claimed: Theorem 6.4(iii) in full, Conjecture 2.1 (convergence of every trajectory), or that any minimality result is formalized in Lean.

Conjecture 2.2 says the proximity digraph is constant after a finite time; Conjecture 2.3 says every trajectory reaches a fixed state or is eventually pseudo-stable (the agents split into two non-empty classes, fixed at their limits or moving strictly towards them from one side); Theorem 6.4(iv) says a trajectory whose digraph is constant from some time on is eventually pseudo-stable. For the four systems of the source (SBC with seven agents and rate -1/6; SBI with seven agents and rate (1 - sqrt 5)/8; SBC with six agents; a second SBI system with seven agents) the development proves the closed form x(t) = x_inf + c lambda^t v for every t, the neighbourhood of every agent at every t (alternating with the parity of t at the middle agent of the two seven-agent alternating systems, the same at every t in the other two), convergence, and that no trajectory is ever frozen or pseudo-stable after any time towards any vector, since four agents alternate sides of their limits. Hence Conjectures 2.2 and 2.3 fail in each model, and Theorem 6.4(iv) fails in each model, both in its literal reading and in the reading that also admits a fixed state. Two smaller constant-digraph systems found in this development, five SBC agents with rate (1 - sqrt 2)/3 and six SBI agents with rate (13 - sqrt 249)/40, have one real negative mode. A five-agent SBI system of this development has a complex pair of modes: the offsets of its three moving agents follow a rational averaging map from an algebraic initial offset (the real root of a cubic), its digraph is constant, it converges, and every moving agent is strictly on both sides of its limit in every five consecutive times. So Conjecture 2.3 and Theorem 6.4(iv) fail with five agents in either model. A five-agent SBC family shows that these failures persist with positive, unequal bounds whose ratio of largest to smallest is below any 1 + epsilon. Along all four source systems the final value at constant topology (Definition 3.1) of every x(t) is the limit, and in the two constant-digraph source systems the per-step convergence factor (Definition 6.1) of every agent with nonzero offset is identically the negative rate, so it converges to no non-negative number. On the positive side, Lemma 4.2 (the equi-topology neighbourhood preserves the proximity digraph) and Lemma 4.8 (a convergent trajectory whose limit has every equi-topology distance positive eventually has the digraph of its limit, the limit as its final value at constant topology, and an equilibrium limit) are proved for arbitrary bounds; the limits of the two constant-digraph systems satisfy that hypothesis, and those of the two alternating systems violate it. For the source's two spectator systems (nine SBC agents with a spectator and two beacons; eight SBI agents with a spectator) the closed forms, the constant tables and the spectator's side are proved, and along the five-agent SBC and six-agent SBI single-mode systems too the final value at constant topology is the limit and the per-step factor is the rate. Not claimed: Theorem 6.4(iii) in full, Conjecture 2.1 (convergence of every trajectory), or that any minimality result is formalized in Lean.

For the four systems of the source (SBC with seven agents and rate -1/6; SBI with seven agents and rate (1 - sqrt 5)/8; SBC with six agents; a second SBI system with seven agents) the development proves the closed form x(t) = x_inf + c lambda^t v for every t, the neighbourhood of every agent at every t (alternating with the parity of t at the middle agent of the two seven-agent alternating systems, the same at every t in the other two), convergence, and that no trajectory is ever frozen or pseudo-stable after any time towards any vector, since four agents alternate sides of their limits. Hence Conjectures 2.2 and 2.3 fail in each model, and Theorem 6.4(iv) fails in each model, both in its literal reading and in the reading that also admits a fixed state. Two smaller constant-digraph systems found in this development, five SBC agents with rate (1 - sqrt 2)/3 and six SBI agents with rate (13 - sqrt 249)/40, have one real negative mode. A five-agent SBI system of this development has a complex pair of modes: the offsets of its three moving agents follow a rational averaging map from an algebraic initial offset (the real root of a cubic), its digraph is constant, it converges, and every moving agent is strictly on both sides of its limit in every five consecutive times. So Conjecture 2.3 and Theorem 6.4(iv) fail with five agents in either model. A five-agent SBC family shows that these failures persist with positive, unequal bounds whose ratio of largest to smallest is below any 1 + epsilon. Along all four source systems the final value at constant topology (Definition 3.1) of every x(t) is the limit, and in the two constant-digraph source systems the per-step convergence factor (Definition 6.1) of every agent with nonzero offset is identically the negative rate, so it converges to no non-negative number. On the positive side, Lemma 4.2 (the equi-topology neighbourhood preserves the proximity digraph) and Lemma 4.8 (a convergent trajectory whose limit has every equi-topology distance positive eventually has the digraph of its limit, the limit as its final value at constant topology, and an equilibrium limit) are proved for arbitrary bounds; the limits of the two constant-digraph systems satisfy that hypothesis, and those of the two alternating systems violate it. For the source's two spectator systems (nine SBC agents with a spectator and two beacons; eight SBI agents with a spectator) the closed forms, the constant tables and the spectator's side are proved, and along the five-agent SBC and six-agent SBI single-mode systems too the final value at constant topology is the limit and the per-step factor is the rate. Not claimed: Theorem 6.4(iii) in full, Conjecture 2.1 (convergence of every trajectory), or that any minimality result is formalized in Lean.

For the four systems of the source (SBC with seven agents and rate -1/6; SBI with seven agents and rate (1 - sqrt 5)/8; SBC with six agents; a second SBI system with seven agents) the development proves the closed form x(t) = x_inf + c lambda^t v for every t, the neighbourhood of every agent at every t (alternating with the parity of t at the middle agent of the two seven-agent alternating systems, the same at every t in the other two), convergence, and that no trajectory is ever frozen or pseudo-stable after any time towards any vector, since four agents alternate sides of their limits. Hence Conjectures 2.2 and 2.3 fail in each model, and Theorem 6.4(iv) fails in each model, both in its literal reading and in the reading that also admits a fixed state. Two smaller constant-digraph systems found in this development, five SBC agents with rate (1 - sqrt 2)/3 and six SBI agents with rate (13 - sqrt 249)/40, have one real negative mode. A five-agent SBI system of this development has a complex pair of modes: the offsets of its three moving agents follow a rational averaging map from an algebraic initial offset (the real root of a cubic), its digraph is constant, it converges, and every moving agent is strictly on both sides of its limit in every five consecutive times. So Conjecture 2.3 and Theorem 6.4(iv) fail with five agents in either model. A five-agent SBC family shows that these failures persist with positive, unequal bounds whose ratio of largest to smallest is below any 1 + epsilon. Along all four source systems the final value at constant topology (Definition 3.1) of every x(t) is the limit, and in the two constant-digraph source systems the per-step convergence factor (Definition 6.1) of every agent with nonzero offset is identically the negative rate, so it converges to no non-negative number. On the positive side, Lemma 4.2 (the equi-topology neighbourhood preserves the proximity digraph) and Lemma 4.8 (a convergent trajectory whose limit has every equi-topology distance positive eventually has the digraph of its limit, the limit as its final value at constant topology, and an equilibrium limit) are proved for arbitrary bounds; the limits of the two constant-digraph systems satisfy that hypothesis, and those of the two alternating systems violate it. For the source's two spectator systems (nine SBC agents with a spectator and two beacons; eight SBI agents with a spectator) the closed forms, the constant tables and the spectator's side are proved, and along the five-agent SBC and six-agent SBI single-mode systems too the final value at constant topology is the limit and the per-step factor is the rate. Not claimed: Theorem 6.4(iii) in full, Conjecture 2.1 (convergence of every trajectory), or that any minimality result is formalized in Lean.

For the four systems of the source (SBC with seven agents and rate -1/6; SBI with seven agents and rate (1 - sqrt 5)/8; SBC with six agents; a second SBI system with seven agents) the development proves the closed form x(t) = x_inf + c lambda^t v for every t, the neighbourhood of every agent at every t (alternating with the parity of t at the middle agent of the two seven-agent alternating systems, the same at every t in the other two), convergence, and that no trajectory is ever frozen or pseudo-stable after any time towards any vector, since four agents alternate sides of their limits. Hence Conjectures 2.2 and 2.3 fail in each model, and Theorem 6.4(iv) fails in each model, both in its literal reading and in the reading that also admits a fixed state. Two smaller constant-digraph systems found in this development, five SBC agents with rate (1 - sqrt 2)/3 and six SBI agents with rate (13 - sqrt 249)/40, have one real negative mode. A five-agent SBI system of this development has a complex pair of modes: the offsets of its three moving agents follow a rational averaging map from an algebraic initial offset (the real root of a cubic), its digraph is constant, it converges, and every moving agent is strictly on both sides of its limit in every five consecutive times. So Conjecture 2.3 and Theorem 6.4(iv) fail with five agents in either model. A five-agent SBC family shows that these failures persist with positive, unequal bounds whose ratio of largest to smallest is below any 1 + epsilon. Along all four source systems the final value at constant topology (Definition 3.1) of every x(t) is the limit, and in the two constant-digraph source systems the per-step convergence factor (Definition 6.1) of every agent with nonzero offset is identically the negative rate, so it converges to no non-negative number. On the positive side, Lemma 4.2 (the equi-topology neighbourhood preserves the proximity digraph) and Lemma 4.8 (a convergent trajectory whose limit has every equi-topology distance positive eventually has the digraph of its limit, the limit as its final value at constant topology, and an equilibrium limit) are proved for arbitrary bounds; the limits of the two constant-digraph systems satisfy that hypothesis, and those of the two alternating systems violate it. For the source's two spectator systems (nine SBC agents with a spectator and two beacons; eight SBI agents with a spectator) the closed forms, the constant tables and the spectator's side are proved, and along the five-agent SBC and six-agent SBI single-mode systems too the final value at constant topology is the limit and the per-step factor is the rate. Not claimed: Theorem 6.4(iii) in full, Conjecture 2.1 (convergence of every trajectory), or that any minimality result is formalized in Lean.

For the four systems of the source (SBC with seven agents and rate -1/6; SBI with seven agents and rate (1 - sqrt 5)/8; SBC with six agents; a second SBI system with seven agents) the development proves the closed form x(t) = x_inf + c lambda^t v for every t, the neighbourhood of every agent at every t (alternating with the parity of t at the middle agent of the two seven-agent alternating systems, the same at every t in the other two), convergence, and that no trajectory is ever frozen or pseudo-stable after any time towards any vector, since four agents alternate sides of their limits. Hence Conjectures 2.2 and 2.3 fail in each model, and Theorem 6.4(iv) fails in each model, both in its literal reading and in the reading that also admits a fixed state. Two smaller constant-digraph systems found in this development, five SBC agents with rate (1 - sqrt 2)/3 and six SBI agents with rate (13 - sqrt 249)/40, have one real negative mode. A five-agent SBI system of this development has a complex pair of modes: the offsets of its three moving agents follow a rational averaging map from an algebraic initial offset (the real root of a cubic), its digraph is constant, it converges, and every moving agent is strictly on both sides of its limit in every five consecutive times. So Conjecture 2.3 and Theorem 6.4(iv) fail with five agents in either model. A five-agent SBC family shows that these failures persist with positive, unequal bounds whose ratio of largest to smallest is below any 1 + epsilon. Along all four source systems the final value at constant topology (Definition 3.1) of every x(t) is the limit, and in the two constant-digraph source systems the per-step convergence factor (Definition 6.1) of every agent with nonzero offset is identically the negative rate, so it converges to no non-negative number. On the positive side, Lemma 4.2 (the equi-topology neighbourhood preserves the proximity digraph) and Lemma 4.8 (a convergent trajectory whose limit has every equi-topology distance positive eventually has the digraph of its limit, the limit as its final value at constant topology, and an equilibrium limit) are proved for arbitrary bounds; the limits of the two constant-digraph systems satisfy that hypothesis, and those of the two alternating systems violate it. For the source's two spectator systems (nine SBC agents with a spectator and two beacons; eight SBI agents with a spectator) the closed forms, the constant tables and the spectator's side are proved, and along the five-agent SBC and six-agent SBI single-mode systems too the final value at constant topology is the limit and the per-step factor is the rate. Not claimed: Theorem 6.4(iii) in full, Conjecture 2.1 (convergence of every trajectory), or that any minimality result is formalized in Lean.

For the four systems of the source (SBC with seven agents and rate -1/6; SBI with seven agents and rate (1 - sqrt 5)/8; SBC with six agents; a second SBI system with seven agents) the development proves the closed form x(t) = x_inf + c lambda^t v for every t, the neighbourhood of every agent at every t (alternating with the parity of t at the middle agent of the two seven-agent alternating systems, the same at every t in the other two), convergence, and that no trajectory is ever frozen or pseudo-stable after any time towards any vector, since four agents alternate sides of their limits. So Conjecture 2.3 and Theorem 6.4(iv) fail with five agents in either model. A five-agent SBC family shows that these failures persist with positive, unequal bounds whose ratio of largest to smallest is below any 1 + epsilon. records.name: Erdos627.erdos_627.variants.tutte_zykov
records.entry_name: Triangle-free graphs with prescribed chromatic number
records.doc: A Lean formalization of the classical existence of finite triangle-free graphs with arbitrarily large chromatic number. For each integer k at least two, it constructs a finite simple graph whose clique number is exactly two and whose chromatic number is exactly k. The proof iterates the Mycielski construction from the complete graph on two vertices. This is the Tutte–Zykov variant recorded with Erdős problem 627, not a solution of that problem's open asymptotic limit question.

records.name: PalomarWE.mathematical_result
records.entry_name: Write-Execute computation: a Lean formalization of Self-Spectre with errata
records.doc: Formalizes Gregory Morse's 2019 paper "Self-Spectre, Write-Execute and the Hidden State": the Write-Execute half unconditionally, the Self-Spectre half as conditional theorems over an abstract speculation contract. An ideal word-level machine whose only operations are a store and a jump, with no data reads, simulates finite Turing machines step for step, preserving halting, divergence and the tape; a finite image is exact until its guard faults. The development proves the jump-table lookup, the 8-bit tables, wide ADD, SUB, SHL, SHR, XOR, 32x32 multiplication, 64/32 division, two-step modular reduction, modular exponentiation with its multiplication count, the AES-128 T-table cipher and the Write-Execute AES procedure against FIPS-197. The Self-Spectre half is proved as a conditional result under an abstract speculation contract (a branch predictor and a speculation window as parameters, rollback of the architectural state, persistence of the cache): the Fig. 1 mistraining schedule, the Fig. 2 victim leak with the mix-order reload from a cleared probe array, the speculation-depth boundary (touch trace for any cache, observable reload hits from a cleared probe array) and the hidden Write-Execute computation. Supporting byte-level x86/x64 models of Figs. 5, 6 and 7 and native vectors for the corrected C and MASM sources accompany the selected statement.

records.name: OAI.EuclideanRamsey.Mobius.ramsey_iff_ramsey_mobius_full
records.entry_name: Möbius invariance of the Ramsey property for finite spherical sets
records.doc: Theorem C: for finitely many distinct points a of the unit sphere of R^d and any L in O(1,d) (L^T S L = S with S = diag(-1, 1, ..., 1)), the configuration a is Euclidean Ramsey if and only if its image under the Möbius map phi_L is Euclidean Ramsey. There is no affine-spanning hypothesis. Ramsey is OpenAI's definition from result 172 (for every r >= 2 there is D such that every r-colouring of R^D contains a monochromatic congruent copy). Corollaries, also proved: every Möbius image of a finite set of distinct unit-sphere points with real algebraic coordinates is Ramsey; and for distinct rationals t_i and arbitrary reals k != 0 and c, the circle points circ(k t_i) and circ(t_i + c) form Ramsey sets, where circ is the stereographic chart of the unit circle. The proof builds on OpenAI's complete Lean proof of the classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations (openai/math fd4aeeb2, result 172), whose 28 files are included with header-only changes for the Lean module system. The Lorentz matrix transports OpenAI's real tensor criterion; OpenAI's descent and sufficiency conclude. All theorems depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.

records.name: PDTSourceSelection.quadraticSelection
records.entry_name: Selection of the electromagnetic source tensor by covariance, conservation and the exchange law
records.doc: On a fixed flat Lorentz frame with metric diag(1,1,1,-1), sources are symmetric 4x4 tensor-valued functions of the six real components of an antisymmetric field. Twelve kernel-checked statements. Among all symmetric homogeneous quadratic sources (210 free coefficients), the six infinitesimal Lorentz covariance equations together with zero trace select the Maxwell stress (the electromagnetic energy-momentum tensor) up to a unique real scale, and a displayed certificate of 209 linear coefficient equations is equivalent to both laws. Among the same homogeneous quadratic sources, conservation alone - vanishing divergence on every source-free Maxwell/Bianchi first jet - selects the same line, with covariance, trace zero and Hodge invariance derived rather than assumed. The globally C^3 symmetric conserved sources are exactly an explicit seventeen-parameter family (constant, a six-parameter cross term, and the stress), and with covariance zero field value is equivalent to zero trace and to the stress line. Under the sourceful exchange law at current stiffness k (the real factor multiplying the jet current), every everywhere-differentiable symmetric source is a constant plus the Maxwell stress of scale exactly k, and conversely, with no polynomial, degree, C^3, covariance or trace hypothesis; zero field value selects the stress. Explicit counterexamples show that covariance and zero trace are each necessary in the quadratic selection, and that covariance and the zero-field normalization are each necessary in the C^3 selection. Uniqueness of the Maxwell stress tensor is classical (Fock 1964; Kerrighan 1982; Navarro-Sancho 2012; the classification of Maxwell conservation laws by Anco-Pohjanpelto 2001); the contribution is the constructive, kernel-checked development on the explicit register at finite regularity, with finite certificates, the covariance-free routes, and the differentiable-only sourceful statement. Pisot Dimensional Theory motivates the frame; no physical coupling is selected.

Among all symmetric homogeneous quadratic sources (210 free coefficients), the six infinitesimal Lorentz covariance equations together with zero trace select the Maxwell stress (the electromagnetic energy-momentum tensor) up to a unique real scale, and a displayed certificate of 209 linear coefficient equations is equivalent to both laws. Among the same homogeneous quadratic sources, conservation alone - vanishing divergence on every source-free Maxwell/Bianchi first jet - selects the same line, with covariance, trace zero and Hodge invariance derived rather than assumed. The globally C^3 symmetric conserved sources are exactly an explicit seventeen-parameter family (constant, a six-parameter cross term, and the stress), and with covariance zero field value is equivalent to zero trace and to the stress line. Under the sourceful exchange law at current stiffness k (the real factor multiplying the jet current), every everywhere-differentiable symmetric source is a constant plus the Maxwell stress of scale exactly k, and conversely, with no polynomial, degree, C^3, covariance or trace hypothesis; zero field value selects the stress. Explicit counterexamples show that covariance and zero trace are each necessary in the quadratic selection, and that covariance and the zero-field normalization are each necessary in the C^3 selection. Uniqueness of the Maxwell stress tensor is classical (Fock 1964; Kerrighan 1982; Navarro-Sancho 2012; the classification of Maxwell conservation laws by Anco-Pohjanpelto 2001); the contribution is the constructive, kernel-checked development on the explicit register at finite regularity, with finite certificates, the covariance-free routes, and the differentiable-only sourceful statement. records.name: OnePhaseDimension.Headline.challenge_flat_of_textbookMin
records.entry_name: Flatness of one-homogeneous one-phase Bernoulli minimizers in dimensions at most six
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the flatness half of the main theorem of the OpenAI preprint "The critical dimension for one-phase Bernoulli minimizers" (September 24, 2026): for 1 ≤ d ≤ 6, every nonnegative, nonzero, one-homogeneous global minimizer u of the one-phase Bernoulli energy J(v; B) = ∫_B |∇v|² + 1_{v > 0} in ℝᵈ is flat, that is, u(x) = max(⟪x, e⟫, 0) for almost every x, for some unit vector e. The minimizer class is the one of Alt and Caffarelli, written out from Mathlib definitions: on every ball B, u ∈ H¹(B) and J(u; B) ≤ J(v; B) for every v ∈ H¹(B) with v − u ∈ H¹₀(B), with weak gradients and H¹₀(B) (the closure of C_c^∞(B)) defined in the statement itself. The proof follows the preprint's universal-certificate method; the classical regularity theory of one-phase minimizers that the preprint cites is proved, in this repository or its dependencies, and the classification in dimensions d ≤ 4, which the preprint cites, is proved by the same exclusion method with new certificates.

records.name: SupportCriterion.normalized_quantitative_gap
records.entry_name: Sharp universal support criterion for sub-Gaussian laws
records.doc: For every Borel probability law on the real line that is symmetric about zero and satisfies 0 < a <= |X| <= b almost surely, the support ratio b/a <= sqrt(3) + sqrt(2) guarantees E exp(t X) <= exp(t^2 E X^2 / 2) for every real t. The inequality is strict for nonzero t, and the actual variance is the optimal quadratic proxy. An explicit symmetric law on {-R,-1,1,R} violates the bound near zero for each larger ratio R. In the normalization 3-sqrt(6) <= X^2 <= 3+sqrt(6), the development also establishes the sharp eighth-order MGF gap with its optimal interiority coefficient, identifies the unique law with Gaussian fourth-moment contact, and proves the sharp global Wasserstein bound for the squared law at every feasible fourth-cumulant deficit, including attainment. The proof combines a convex endpoint reduction, control of the entire moment tail, exact rational Bernstein certificates, and an explicit affine transport coupling.

records.name: Smirnov.exists_sigmaLocallyFiniteBasis_of_pointFinite_open_cover
records.entry_name: Smirnov's local-to-global metrization theorem
records.doc: A space is metrizable if and only if it is Hausdorff, paracompact and locally metrizable. A reusable construction gives a sigma locally finite basis from any point-finite open cover of metrizable patches in a paracompact space, without a separation hypothesis. Local neighborhoods, the cover index and each basis layer may have arbitrary cardinality. The proof assumes no second countability, separability, local compactness or nonemptiness. Classical mathematics; no novelty or priority claim.

records.name: HaggkvistJanssen.exists_listEdgeColoring_complete
records.entry_name: The Häggkvist–Janssen bound on the list chromatic index of complete graphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Häggkvist–Janssen theorem χ′ₗ(Kₙ) ≤ n: for arbitrary lists of at least n colours on the edges of the complete graph on n vertices (from an arbitrary colour type), there is a proper edge colouring, i.e. a colouring of Mathlib's line graph of ⊤, choosing every colour from the list of its edge. Orders 0 and 1 are included. The proof constructs an explicit local-rank certificate, shows by a forced-choice induction that the corresponding coefficient of an extended-star polynomial is nonzero, and applies Mathlib's combinatorial Nullstellensatz; it is an alternative presentation, not a literal translation of the article's argument.

records.name: Vizing.lineGraph_colorable
records.entry_name: Vizing's theorem and equitable edge colourings
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Vizing's theorem: every finite simple graph G has a proper edge colouring with Δ(G) + 1 colours, stated with Mathlib's line graph (G.lineGraph is (Δ(G) + 1)-colourable, hence χ'(G) ≤ Δ(G) + 1), proved with fans and Kempe chain exchanges. It also proves the equitable refinement: for every c ≥ Δ(G) + 1 there is a proper edge colouring with colours Fin c in which any two colour classes (including unused colours) differ in size by at most one (McDiarmid 1972), obtained by balancing a Vizing colouring with alternating-component moves that strictly decrease a square energy.

records.name: PlanarChoosability.isPlanar_iff_minorFree
records.entry_name: Wagner's planarity criterion and list colouring of planar and K5-minor-free graphs
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of classical results on planar graphs and graphs without a K5 minor. (1) Wagner's theorem (1937): a finite graph is planar if and only if it has neither K5 nor K3,3 as a minor. (2) Škrekovski's theorem (1998): every finite graph without a K5 minor is 5-choosable, proved along the route of Wood and Linusson, and Thomassen's theorem (1994) that every finite planar graph is 5-choosable, as a corollary. (3) DP-colouring: every finite graph without a K5 minor (Li–Wang, 2022), hence every finite planar graph (Dvořák–Postle, 2018), is DP-5-colourable. (4) Voigt's theorem (1993): an explicit planar graph on 238 vertices with lists of four colours has no proper list colouring, so 5 cannot be lowered to 4; its planarity and non-colourability are checked by kernel reduction. (5) Wagner's equivalence of the Four Colour Theorem with Hadwiger's conjecture for K5 (neither side is proved). Planarity is defined combinatorially, by rotation systems of genus zero (Euler defect 0); as sanity checks K4 is planar and K5, K3,3 are not.

records.name: Erdos415.finite_counterexample826
records.entry_name: A finite counterexample for strict consecutive totient patterns
records.doc: Formalizes the finite counterexample at cutoff 826 from Proposition 1.2 of Przemek Chojecki's Consecutive Totient Patterns. With ranks assigned to positions and an inclusive cutoff, every strict length-three permutation occurs, no increasing length-four block occurs, and a decreasing length-four block does occur. Hence the largest universal length is three and decreasing is not always absent at the first non-universal length. This is a partial negative result for a specified reading of Erdos Problem 415; no novelty, asymptotic result or natural weak-order frequency result is claimed.

records.name: BrownianImages.audit_main
records.entry_name: Distinguishing sets and measures from their planar Brownian images
records.doc: Lean 4 formalisation of all 32 numbered statements of "Distinguishing sets and measures from their planar Brownian images" (Sascha Troscheit, arXiv:2610.16339), which asks whether two deterministic time measures on the unit interval can be distinguished almost surely from a single planar Brownian image. Rescaled correlation integrals of the time measures determine expected correlation profiles of the image measures, and profiles that differ in the limit make the image laws mutually singular, even when the time measures have the same dimension. For natural measures of self-similar sets satisfying the open set condition, renewal theory gives the profile asymptotics, a limit in the non-lattice case and a periodic non-constant limit in the lattice case, which separates lattice from non-lattice measures. Normalised neighbourhood measures of the compact Brownian image converge almost surely to the occupation measure, so the separation transfers to the laws of the compact image sets. In the two-contraction family of fixed dimension, the mean profile is real analytic and non-constant in the parameter, so each parameter is separated from all but finitely many others; for sufficiently small dimension the mean is strictly increasing and every pair of distinct parameters is separated. A homometric pair of self-similar measures with non-isometric attractors and identical profiles shows that the profile does not determine the measure. Renewal theory is proved for the self-similar laws used, and the nine headline results are stated over Mathlib alone and audited with Comparator.

records.name: DrossTriangle.dross_fractional_triangle_decomposition
records.entry_name: Dross's theorem on fractional triangle decompositions
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Dross's theorem: every finite graph on n vertices with minimum degree at least 9n/10 has a fractional triangle decomposition, i.e. nonnegative real weights on its triangles such that every edge lies in triangles of total weight exactly one. The threshold 9/10 is the exact one of the paper. The proof follows the max-flow/min-cut approach: the existence of the weights is reduced to a flow problem, a finite max-flow/min-cut theorem (included) is applied, and every cut is bounded below by counting triangles and K4s, with a peeling reduction for heavy triangles.

records.name: BeckFiala.exists_rounding
records.entry_name: The Beck–Fiala integer-making theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Beck–Fiala integer-making theorem in its rational unit-cube form: if A is a 0/1 matrix in which every column has at most t ≥ 1 ones and x ∈ [0,1]^N has rational coordinates, then x can be rounded to y ∈ {0,1}^N with |∑ᵢ A j i (y i − x i)| < t for every row j; moreover the rounding can keep every coordinate of x that is already 0 or 1. The proof is the floating-coordinates argument: while some coordinates are strictly between 0 and 1, the rows with more than t floating coordinates are fewer than the floating coordinates, so a nonzero direction keeps their sums fixed, and moving along it makes a coordinate integral; induction on the number of floating coordinates.

records.name: Darpa018.MatrixSquareZero.units_map_surjective_of_squareZeroKernel
records.entry_name: H2 obstruction to lifting discrete matrix representations
records.doc: A Lean proof that a discrete matrix representation lifts across a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings with square-zero kernel exactly when its explicitly constructed second-cohomology obstruction vanishes. The proof constructs the conjugation action and defect cocycle for an abelian group extension, proves the lifting criterion, and applies it to reduction of invertible matrices. The underlying additive kernel is identified with matrices over the coefficient-ring kernel. This is classical obstruction theory motivated by DARPA Challenge 18, not a solution of its homotopy/Langlands research agenda.

records.name: AsymptoticTrianglePacking.near_regular_nibble
records.entry_name: Near-regular hypergraph matchings and the asymptotic triangle-packing gap
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of three results. (1) A finite nibble theorem: r-uniform hypergraphs whose degrees are at most (1+μ)d everywhere and at least (1−μ)d outside an exceptional set of at most η|V| vertices, with codegrees at most μd, have matchings with at least (1−β)|V|/r edges. (2) The fractional–integral triangle-packing gap is o(n²) uniformly over finite graphs: every large graph has an edge-disjoint triangle family P such that every fractional triangle packing has weight at most |P| + εn² (the triangle case of Haxell–Rödl). (3) The cover form: a fractional triangle cover of weight at most |P| + εn² exists. The proof combines a nibble with second-moment and Freedman-type concentration, a low-degree core reduction, Mathlib's Szemerédi regularity lemma with a cluster linear program rounded by explicit designs, and LP duality.

records.name: Palomar.garding
records.entry_name: Solvability of divergence-form elliptic equations (Evans §6.2)
records.doc:
A Lean 4 formalisation of the solvability theory of linear second-order elliptic operators in divergence form on a bounded domain,

  -div(A grad u) + b · grad u + c u = f in Ω,   u = 0 on ∂Ω,

with A uniformly elliptic and every coefficient bounded and measurable. The drift b is unrestricted and the bilinear form is in general non-symmetric. The six compared statements are the results of Evans §6.2: the Gårding inequality, existence and uniqueness of the weak solution with no drift and a nonnegative zeroth-order coefficient, the Fredholm alternative, solvability against the transpose problem, the discrete set of exceptional shifts and boundedness of the inverse. They ask only that Ω be bounded and open, and the compact embedding of H_0^1(Ω) in L²(Ω) is proved. Interior regularity at every order, the maximum principles and the Dirichlet eigenvalue sequence are also proved in the library and appear without a Comparator configuration. Built on Mathlib with only Lean's standard axioms.

records.entry_name: Solvability of divergence-form elliptic equations (Evans §6.2)
records.doc:
A Lean 4 formalisation of the solvability theory of linear second-order elliptic operators in divergence form on a bounded domain,

  -div(A grad u) + b · grad u + c u = f in Ω,   u = 0 on ∂Ω,

with A uniformly elliptic and every coefficient bounded and measurable. The drift b is unrestricted and the bilinear form is in general non-symmetric. The six compared statements are the results of Evans §6.2: the Gårding inequality, existence and uniqueness of the weak solution with no drift and a nonnegative zeroth-order coefficient, the Fredholm alternative, solvability against the transpose problem, the discrete set of exceptional shifts and boundedness of the inverse. They ask only that Ω be bounded and open, and the compact embedding of H_0^1(Ω) in L²(Ω) is proved. Interior regularity at every order, the maximum principles and the Dirichlet eigenvalue sequence are also proved in the library and appear without a Comparator configuration. records.name: positive_density_collatz_reaches_one
records.entry_name: CollatzPosDens
records.doc: `CollatzPosDens` is a formal proof of the main results of *Explicit positive lower density for the Collatz Conjecture* (hexagon:2610.00249). records.name: EvenOrderMDS.maximum_length_of_MDS_code
records.entry_name: The MDS conjecture over finite fields of even order
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof of the linear MDS conjecture for every finite field of even order. For a finite field K with an even number q of elements and 2 ≤ k ≤ q, the maximum length of a k-dimensional linear maximum distance separable (MDS) code over K is q + 2 when k = 3 or k = q − 1, and q + 1 otherwise; codes are subspaces of K^N and an MDS code is one whose minimum Hamming distance equals N − k + 1. The upper bound is proved through the correspondence between MDS codes and arcs: after puncturing and duality it suffices to exclude arcs of q + 2 vectors in K^r for 4 ≤ r ≤ q/2 + 1. A hypothetical such arc gives one plane arc together with r − 3 lifts that, with three coordinate rows, form r linearly independent vectors; the formalization proves that all lifts of a plane arc lie in one common subspace of dimension at most r − 1. The proof uses an exactly normalized form of Segre's envelope of the tangents, a characteristic-two derivative obstruction, and a dimension bound for a colon ideal of (X^n, Y^n, Z^n) with n = q/2. Extended Reed–Solomon codes and the regular hyperoval show that the bound is attained.

records.name: LocalBN.edgeLocalizedNoncompleteUnordered
records.entry_name: Localized two-eigenvalue bound for finite noncomplete graphs
records.doc: For every finite noncomplete simple graph with at least two vertices, the sum of the squares of its two largest ordered adjacency eigenvalues is bounded by the sum over unordered edges of 2(1-1/c(e)), where c(e) is the largest clique containing the edge. The proof establishes the concrete edge-clique scalar certificate and transfers it through the checked BN completely positive spectral lift. Connectedness is unnecessary.

records.name: PerfectImage.exists_radius_star_subset
records.entry_name: Perfect images of metrizable spaces
records.doc: Every continuous closed surjection with compact fibers from an arbitrary metrizable space has a metrizable codomain. A new uniform shrinking-star estimate for compact-fiber metric neighborhoods constructs a sigma locally finite open basis on the image. A proper-map formulation and an actual compatible metric are included. No second countability, separability, compact domain, local compactness, completeness, finite-fiber or nonemptiness assumption is made. Target separation is derived. Classical mathematics; no novelty or priority claim.

records.name: Crystallographic.psi_eq_zero_iff
records.entry_name: The crystallographic restriction in every dimension: GL(N, ℤ) has an element of order m if and only if ψ(m) ≤ N
records.doc: A Lean 4 development of the crystallographic restriction in every dimension. For a positive integer m let psi(m) be the sum of phi(p^k) over the prime powers p^k exactly dividing m, except that the prime power 2 contributes 0 (phi is Euler's totient; psi(1) = psi(2) = 0, psi(3) = psi(4) = psi(6) = 2, psi(ab) = psi(a) + psi(b) for coprime a, b; OEIS A080737). Theorem (Vaidyanathaswamy 1928; Hiller 1985; a proof in Kuzmanovich-Pavlichenkov 2002; Theorem 1 of Bamberg-Cairns-Kilminster 2003): for N >= 1, the group GL(N, Z) of invertible integer N x N matrices has an element of order m >= 1 if and only if psi(m) <= N. The development proves both directions: necessity through the minimal polynomial of the matrix over Q, which divides X^m - 1 and is therefore a product of distinct cyclotomic polynomials whose indices have least common multiple m, so that psi(m) is at most its degree; sufficiency by one block of size phi(p^k) for each prime power p^k != 2 of m (multiplication by the root on Z[X]/(Phi_{p^k}) in its power basis), the sign -1 when m is 2 modulo 4, and an identity block. Corollaries: the finite orders of GL(N, Z) are the positive m with psi(m) <= N; the least dimension carrying an element of order m is psi(m), or 1 for m = 2 (OEIS A152455); GL(phi(n), Z) has an element of order n for every n >= 1; the same equivalence holds for GL(N, Q); GL(0, Z) has only the order 1 and the finite orders grow with the dimension; GL(N + 1, Z) has the same finite orders as GL(N, Z) for even N >= 2; the set of finite orders is finite and bounded by 2^(N + 1). The arithmetic of psi: psi(m) = 0 iff m <= 2; psi(p^k) = phi(p^k) for a prime power p^k != 2; additivity on coprime factors; psi <= phi; psi is even; psi as a sum over the exact prime-power divisors; m <= 2^(psi(m) + 1). The tables of finite orders for N = 1, ..., 12 (OEIS A080738) and the largest finite order 2, 6, 12, 30, 60, 120, 210 in dimensions 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 are proved by the bound and a kernel computation of psi. Beyond dimension 12, the eleven orders 2520 (psi = 20), 2310 (psi = 22) and 2184, 2340, 2640, 2730, 2772, 3080, 3960, 4620, 5040 (psi = 24), which rows 20, 22 and 24 of Table 1 of Bamberg-Cairns-Kilminster omit, are checked with their least dimensions. The same equivalence holds in SL(N, Z) for N >= 2 (an element of odd order has determinant 1; the block for 2^k, k >= 2, has even size and determinant 1; -A keeps the determinant in even dimension), and SL(1, Z) is trivial. Every even number is psi(m) for an odd squarefree m (Proposition 3(2) of Bamberg-Cairns-Kilminster and its proof), so for N, M >= 1 the finite orders of GL(N, Z) are among those of GL(M, Z) iff N / 2 <= M / 2 (integer division); each A in GL(N, Z) of finite order m preserves a symmetric integral form, positive definite on integer and real vectors (the proof takes sum_{k<m} (A^k)^T A^k), so psi(m) <= N is also the condition for an element of order m of GL(N, Z) preserving a positive definite integral form; and GL(N, Z) has an element of order m >= 1 and determinant -1 iff m is even and psi(m) + 1 <= N, so the least such dimension is psi(m) + 1 for even m (also over Q). The hypotheses N >= 1 and m >= 1 are necessary and explicit: GL(0, Z) is trivial while psi(2) = 0, and orderOf is 0 at infinite order. The theorem is the standard description of the finite orders of integer matrices, used in the crystallography of higher-dimensional lattices and quasicrystals and in integral representation theory; Mathlib's docs/1000.yaml (Q3527223) and mathlib4 issue #6091 (item 60) list it unformalized, and as of 2026-10-09 no formalization in every dimension, in either direction, was located in the registry, Mathlib, the Lean repositories searched, the Isabelle AFP or arXiv. Not claimed: priority for the two- and three-dimensional cases (public Lean proofs of the case N = 2 exist), the wallpaper or space groups, the isometry group of a given lattice or form, or integral conjugacy.

records.doc: A Lean 4 development of the crystallographic restriction in every dimension. For a positive integer m let psi(m) be the sum of phi(p^k) over the prime powers p^k exactly dividing m, except that the prime power 2 contributes 0 (phi is Euler's totient; psi(1) = psi(2) = 0, psi(3) = psi(4) = psi(6) = 2, psi(ab) = psi(a) + psi(b) for coprime a, b; OEIS A080737). Theorem (Vaidyanathaswamy 1928; Hiller 1985; a proof in Kuzmanovich-Pavlichenkov 2002; Theorem 1 of Bamberg-Cairns-Kilminster 2003): for N >= 1, the group GL(N, Z) of invertible integer N x N matrices has an element of order m >= 1 if and only if psi(m) <= N. The development proves both directions: necessity through the minimal polynomial of the matrix over Q, which divides X^m - 1 and is therefore a product of distinct cyclotomic polynomials whose indices have least common multiple m, so that psi(m) is at most its degree; sufficiency by one block of size phi(p^k) for each prime power p^k != 2 of m (multiplication by the root on Z[X]/(Phi_{p^k}) in its power basis), the sign -1 when m is 2 modulo 4, and an identity block. Corollaries: the finite orders of GL(N, Z) are the positive m with psi(m) <= N; the least dimension carrying an element of order m is psi(m), or 1 for m = 2 (OEIS A152455); GL(phi(n), Z) has an element of order n for every n >= 1; the same equivalence holds for GL(N, Q); GL(0, Z) has only the order 1 and the finite orders grow with the dimension; GL(N + 1, Z) has the same finite orders as GL(N, Z) for even N >= 2; the set of finite orders is finite and bounded by 2^(N + 1). The arithmetic of psi: psi(m) = 0 iff m <= 2; psi(p^k) = phi(p^k) for a prime power p^k != 2; additivity on coprime factors; psi <= phi; psi is even; psi as a sum over the exact prime-power divisors; m <= 2^(psi(m) + 1). The tables of finite orders for N = 1, ..., 12 (OEIS A080738) and the largest finite order 2, 6, 12, 30, 60, 120, 210 in dimensions 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 are proved by the bound and a kernel computation of psi. Beyond dimension 12, the eleven orders 2520 (psi = 20), 2310 (psi = 22) and 2184, 2340, 2640, 2730, 2772, 3080, 3960, 4620, 5040 (psi = 24), which rows 20, 22 and 24 of Table 1 of Bamberg-Cairns-Kilminster omit, are checked with their least dimensions. The same equivalence holds in SL(N, Z) for N >= 2 (an element of odd order has determinant 1; the block for 2^k, k >= 2, has even size and determinant 1; -A keeps the determinant in even dimension), and SL(1, Z) is trivial. Every even number is psi(m) for an odd squarefree m (Proposition 3(2) of Bamberg-Cairns-Kilminster and its proof), so for N, M >= 1 the finite orders of GL(N, Z) are among those of GL(M, Z) iff N / 2 <= M / 2 (integer division); each A in GL(N, Z) of finite order m preserves a symmetric integral form, positive definite on integer and real vectors (the proof takes sum_{k<m} (A^k)^T A^k), so psi(m) <= N is also the condition for an element of order m of GL(N, Z) preserving a positive definite integral form; and GL(N, Z) has an element of order m >= 1 and determinant -1 iff m is even and psi(m) + 1 <= N, so the least such dimension is psi(m) + 1 for even m (also over Q). The hypotheses N >= 1 and m >= 1 are necessary and explicit: GL(0, Z) is trivial while psi(2) = 0, and orderOf is 0 at infinite order. The theorem is the standard description of the finite orders of integer matrices, used in the crystallography of higher-dimensional lattices and quasicrystals and in integral representation theory; Mathlib's docs/1000.yaml (Q3527223) and mathlib4 issue #6091 (item 60) list it unformalized, and as of 2026-10-09 no formalization in every dimension, in either direction, was located in the registry, Mathlib, the Lean repositories searched, the Isabelle AFP or arXiv. Not claimed: priority for the two- and three-dimensional cases (public Lean proofs of the case N = 2 exist), the wallpaper or space groups, the isometry group of a given lattice or form, or integral conjugacy.

For a positive integer m let psi(m) be the sum of phi(p^k) over the prime powers p^k exactly dividing m, except that the prime power 2 contributes 0 (phi is Euler's totient; psi(1) = psi(2) = 0, psi(3) = psi(4) = psi(6) = 2, psi(ab) = psi(a) + psi(b) for coprime a, b; OEIS A080737). Theorem (Vaidyanathaswamy 1928; Hiller 1985; a proof in Kuzmanovich-Pavlichenkov 2002; Theorem 1 of Bamberg-Cairns-Kilminster 2003): for N >= 1, the group GL(N, Z) of invertible integer N x N matrices has an element of order m >= 1 if and only if psi(m) <= N. The development proves both directions: necessity through the minimal polynomial of the matrix over Q, which divides X^m - 1 and is therefore a product of distinct cyclotomic polynomials whose indices have least common multiple m, so that psi(m) is at most its degree; sufficiency by one block of size phi(p^k) for each prime power p^k != 2 of m (multiplication by the root on Z[X]/(Phi_{p^k}) in its power basis), the sign -1 when m is 2 modulo 4, and an identity block. Corollaries: the finite orders of GL(N, Z) are the positive m with psi(m) <= N; the least dimension carrying an element of order m is psi(m), or 1 for m = 2 (OEIS A152455); GL(phi(n), Z) has an element of order n for every n >= 1; the same equivalence holds for GL(N, Q); GL(0, Z) has only the order 1 and the finite orders grow with the dimension; GL(N + 1, Z) has the same finite orders as GL(N, Z) for even N >= 2; the set of finite orders is finite and bounded by 2^(N + 1). The arithmetic of psi: psi(m) = 0 iff m <= 2; psi(p^k) = phi(p^k) for a prime power p^k != 2; additivity on coprime factors; psi <= phi; psi is even; psi as a sum over the exact prime-power divisors; m <= 2^(psi(m) + 1). The tables of finite orders for N = 1, ..., 12 (OEIS A080738) and the largest finite order 2, 6, 12, 30, 60, 120, 210 in dimensions 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 are proved by the bound and a kernel computation of psi. Beyond dimension 12, the eleven orders 2520 (psi = 20), 2310 (psi = 22) and 2184, 2340, 2640, 2730, 2772, 3080, 3960, 4620, 5040 (psi = 24), which rows 20, 22 and 24 of Table 1 of Bamberg-Cairns-Kilminster omit, are checked with their least dimensions. The same equivalence holds in SL(N, Z) for N >= 2 (an element of odd order has determinant 1; the block for 2^k, k >= 2, has even size and determinant 1; -A keeps the determinant in even dimension), and SL(1, Z) is trivial. Every even number is psi(m) for an odd squarefree m (Proposition 3(2) of Bamberg-Cairns-Kilminster and its proof), so for N, M >= 1 the finite orders of GL(N, Z) are among those of GL(M, Z) iff N / 2 <= M / 2 (integer division); each A in GL(N, Z) of finite order m preserves a symmetric integral form, positive definite on integer and real vectors (the proof takes sum_{k<m} (A^k)^T A^k), so psi(m) <= N is also the condition for an element of order m of GL(N, Z) preserving a positive definite integral form; and GL(N, Z) has an element of order m >= 1 and determinant -1 iff m is even and psi(m) + 1 <= N, so the least such dimension is psi(m) + 1 for even m (also over Q). The hypotheses N >= 1 and m >= 1 are necessary and explicit: GL(0, Z) is trivial while psi(2) = 0, and orderOf is 0 at infinite order. The theorem is the standard description of the finite orders of integer matrices, used in the crystallography of higher-dimensional lattices and quasicrystals and in integral representation theory; Mathlib's docs/1000.yaml (Q3527223) and mathlib4 issue #6091 (item 60) list it unformalized, and as of 2026-10-09 no formalization in every dimension, in either direction, was located in the registry, Mathlib, the Lean repositories searched, the Isabelle AFP or arXiv. Not claimed: priority for the two- and three-dimensional cases (public Lean proofs of the case N = 2 exist), the wallpaper or space groups, the isometry group of a given lattice or form, or integral conjugacy.

Corollaries: the finite orders of GL(N, Z) are the positive m with psi(m) <= N; the least dimension carrying an element of order m is psi(m), or 1 for m = 2 (OEIS A152455); GL(phi(n), Z) has an element of order n for every n >= 1; the same equivalence holds for GL(N, Q); GL(0, Z) has only the order 1 and the finite orders grow with the dimension; GL(N + 1, Z) has the same finite orders as GL(N, Z) for even N >= 2; the set of finite orders is finite and bounded by 2^(N + 1). The arithmetic of psi: psi(m) = 0 iff m <= 2; psi(p^k) = phi(p^k) for a prime power p^k != 2; additivity on coprime factors; psi <= phi; psi is even; psi as a sum over the exact prime-power divisors; m <= 2^(psi(m) + 1). The tables of finite orders for N = 1, ..., 12 (OEIS A080738) and the largest finite order 2, 6, 12, 30, 60, 120, 210 in dimensions 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 are proved by the bound and a kernel computation of psi. Beyond dimension 12, the eleven orders 2520 (psi = 20), 2310 (psi = 22) and 2184, 2340, 2640, 2730, 2772, 3080, 3960, 4620, 5040 (psi = 24), which rows 20, 22 and 24 of Table 1 of Bamberg-Cairns-Kilminster omit, are checked with their least dimensions. The same equivalence holds in SL(N, Z) for N >= 2 (an element of odd order has determinant 1; the block for 2^k, k >= 2, has even size and determinant 1; -A keeps the determinant in even dimension), and SL(1, Z) is trivial. Every even number is psi(m) for an odd squarefree m (Proposition 3(2) of Bamberg-Cairns-Kilminster and its proof), so for N, M >= 1 the finite orders of GL(N, Z) are among those of GL(M, Z) iff N / 2 <= M / 2 (integer division); each A in GL(N, Z) of finite order m preserves a symmetric integral form, positive definite on integer and real vectors (the proof takes sum_{k<m} (A^k)^T A^k), so psi(m) <= N is also the condition for an element of order m of GL(N, Z) preserving a positive definite integral form; and GL(N, Z) has an element of order m >= 1 and determinant -1 iff m is even and psi(m) + 1 <= N, so the least such dimension is psi(m) + 1 for even m (also over Q). The hypotheses N >= 1 and m >= 1 are necessary and explicit: GL(0, Z) is trivial while psi(2) = 0, and orderOf is 0 at infinite order. The theorem is the standard description of the finite orders of integer matrices, used in the crystallography of higher-dimensional lattices and quasicrystals and in integral representation theory; Mathlib's docs/1000.yaml (Q3527223) and mathlib4 issue #6091 (item 60) list it unformalized, and as of 2026-10-09 no formalization in every dimension, in either direction, was located in the registry, Mathlib, the Lean repositories searched, the Isabelle AFP or arXiv. records.name: KuratowskiTheorem.isPlanar_K4
records.entry_name: Kuratowski's theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Kuratowski's theorem: a finite graph is planar if and only if it contains no subdivision of K5 and no subdivision of K3,3. Planarity is the combinatorial notion (a rotation system of genus zero). The proof combines Wagner's minor characterization (from the author's planarity library) with three new lemmas: a subdivision of any finite graph H gives H as a minor; a K3,3 minor gives a K3,3 subdivision; a K5 minor gives a K5 or a K3,3 subdivision. The last two rest on joining up to four terminals inside a connected branch set to one centre or to two adjacent centres by internally disjoint paths.

records.name: KonigEdgeColouring.lineGraph_colorable
records.entry_name: Kőnig's theorems and Dilworth's theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Kőnig's edge-colouring theorem: the line graph of a finite bipartite graph G is Δ(G)-colourable, and its chromatic number (the chromatic index of G) equals Δ(G). The proof colours edges one at a time with partial proper edge colourings, recolouring by an a/b Kempe-chain swap whose correctness rests on a parity argument in the bipartite graph; the lower bound comes from the edges at a vertex of maximum degree, which are pairwise adjacent in the line graph. Also formalized: the Kőnig–Egerváry theorem (a finite bipartite graph has a matching and a vertex cover of the same size, via Hall's theorem with deficiency, plus weak duality for all finite graphs), Dilworth's theorem (an antichain A and a partition into |A| chains, by Galvin's induction) and Mirsky's dual theorem (a chain C and a partition into |C| antichains, by the height function).

records.name: MengerTheorem.card_le_of_separates
records.entry_name: Menger's theorem and Hamiltonian cycles
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Menger's theorem for finite graphs (set form with a minimum separator and as many vertex-disjoint paths, two-vertex form, edge form for Mathlib's IsEdgeReachable, and the global edge form for Mathlib's IsEdgeConnected) and of classical sufficient conditions for Hamiltonian cycles: the Bondy–Chvátal closure step, Ore's and Dirac's theorems, and the Chvátal–Erdős theorem (k-connected with independence number at most k implies Hamiltonian), whose proof uses Menger's theorem through the fan lemma.

records.name: RamseyGraphs.ramsey_three_three_upper
records.entry_name: Classical bounds for graph Ramsey numbers
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the classical bounds for graph Ramsey numbers: R(3, 3) = 6 (every graph on six vertices has a triangle or three independent vertices, and the pentagon has neither), the Erdős–Szekeres upper bound R(s, t) ≤ C(s + t − 2, s − 1), and Erdős's lower bound R(k, k) > 2^(k/2) for k ≥ 3, proved by a union bound over the edge sets of graphs on n vertices.

records.name: HadwigerMader.mader
records.entry_name: Mader's theorem and Hadwiger's conjecture for t ≤ 4
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Mader's theorem (a nonempty finite graph of average degree at least 2^(r−2) has a K_r minor), of Dirac's lemma (a graph without a K4 minor has a vertex of degree at most two, hence at most 2n − 3 edges for n ≥ 2), and of Hadwiger's conjecture for t ≤ 4 (graphs without a K3 minor are 2-colourable, graphs without a K4 minor are 3-colourable). Minors are branch-set models.

records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Mader's theorem (a nonempty finite graph of average degree at least 2^(r−2) has a K_r minor), of Dirac's lemma (a graph without a K4 minor has a vertex of degree at most two, hence at most 2n − 3 edges for n ≥ 2), and of Hadwiger's conjecture for t ≤ 4 (graphs without a K3 minor are 2-colourable, graphs without a K4 minor are 3-colourable). Minors are branch-set models.

records.name: RankCertificates.infiniteGeometricClasses_exactRanksFiveThroughSeven
records.entry_name: Elliptic curves of exact ranks five, six, and seven: conditional formalization
records.doc: Lean proves that the finite-complexity affine-linear prime asymptotic implies infinitely many geometric isomorphism classes of rational elliptic curves of each exact Mordell–Weil rank five, six, and seven. The generic analytic theorem is an explicit hypothesis. The specialization checks, two-isogeny descent, exact rank calculations, and passage to infinitely many j-invariants are formalized; the prime asymptotic is not proved in Lean here.

records.name: BrooksColouring.colorable_of_cliqueFree
records.entry_name: Brooks' theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Brooks' theorem: for k ≥ 3, a finite graph of maximum degree at most k without a (k+1)-clique is k-colourable (no connectedness assumption), and a finite connected graph that is neither complete nor an odd cycle is colourable with as many colours as its maximum degree. The proof uses greedy colourings in Lovász's style and an induction on the number of edges with a separation-and-gluing step.

records.name: PetersenMatching.exists_isPerfectMatching
records.entry_name: Petersen's theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Petersen's theorem: a finite 3-regular graph in which no edge is a bridge has a perfect matching; moreover, every edge of such a graph lies in some perfect matching. Both statements are derived from Tutte's theorem (in Mathlib) by counting the edges that leave the odd components.

records.name: Superorthogonal.CDW.sqfct_estimate_of_superorthogonal
records.entry_name: Formalization of a sharp cone square-function estimate via superorthogonality
records.doc:
This is a Lean 4 formalization of Theorems 1.1 and 1.4 from the paper "Diameter-free reverse inequalities and superorthogonality" by A. Cushman, C. Demeter and S. Wu.
Theorem 1.1 is a reverse square-function estimate in L^4 under a superorthogonality hypothesis that is weaker than the Type IV superorthogonality of Gressman-Pierce-Roos-Yung.
Theorem 1.4 applies a similar estimate to the three-dimensional light cone, yielding a refinement of the reverse cone square-function estimate of Guth-Wang-Zhang.

records.name: hilbert_smith
records.entry_name: Hilbert–Smith and p-adic exclusion with second countability
records.doc: A Lean formalization of the Hilbert–Smith statement for a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff topological group acting continuously and faithfully on a connected, Hausdorff, second-countable, finite-dimensional topological manifold. The conclusion gives a smooth real Lie-group structure for the group's existing topology. The development also proves p-adic exclusion for second-countable manifolds and provides universe-polymorphic versions. No second-countability hypothesis is dropped.

records.name: ContinuumIndependence.independence_of_CH
records.entry_name: Continuum hypothesis independence: a Flypitch reproduction
records.doc: An attributed adaptation of the Flypitch formal proof of two-sided syntactic independence of the continuum hypothesis from its explicitly encoded first-order ZFC theory. Cohen and collapse Boolean-valued models, together with soundness, establish that neither the encoded CH sentence nor its negation is derivable. The development uses an expanded language with definable set operations, collection and Zorn's lemma. It does not supply a formal translation to membership-only ZFC or determine the truth of CH for the ambient Lean reals. This is a reproduction of established work, not a new mathematical solution.

records.name: RestrictedSumsetsAudit.counterexample_main
records.entry_name: Counterexamples to the restricted-sumset inverse theorem in arXiv:2609.10148v2
records.doc: Explicit finite counterexamples to Theorem A (Theorem 3.1) and Lemma 3.2 of Li and Liang, arXiv:2609.10148v2. In Z/13Z, sets of sizes seven and four satisfy all size hypotheses and have restricted sumset size nine, but neither is an arithmetic progression. A separate example in Z/11Z contradicts the lower bound of Lemma 3.2 as stated.

records.name: ModalDepth.Contracts.uniform_classification
records.entry_name: Depth-labeled interpolation and substitution in Sacchetti's modal logics
records.doc: Classifies depth labelings in the modal logics wGL_n for positive n. Every simultaneous formula-valued substitution indexed by atom and depth label preserves theoremhood exactly when the labels satisfy c(k+n)=c(k) at every positive depth k. The interpolation equivalences identify the corresponding labeled property with its ordinary interpolation property and the same periodicity condition; the ordinary interpolation theorems remain explicit inputs. Further results classify period spectra, boxed-atom implications and composition of depth substitutions, and transfer a supplied ordinary interpolant while preserving syntax-tree node count and modal depth.

records.name: Erdos99.erdos99_finite_multiplicity
records.entry_name: Erdos 99 Partial Solution
records.doc: A formalization of a partial solution to Erdos Problem 99. It shows that Erdos Problem 99 holds for all sufficiently large n where h(n) is finite. Here, h(n) denotes the number of incongruence, diameter-minimizing sets of minimum separation at least 1.

records.name: BergeTheorem.isMaximum_iff_not_exists_augmenting
records.entry_name: Berge's theorem and the Tutte–Berge formula
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Berge's augmenting path theorem (a matching is maximum if and only if there is no augmenting path) and of the Tutte–Berge formula (the maximum size of a matching is the minimum over vertex sets U of (|V| + |U| − odd(G − U)) / 2), with the weak inequality for all matchings and vertex sets; the formula is derived from Mathlib's Tutte theorem by adding universal vertices.

records.name: BergeTheorem.two_mul_card_add_le
records.entry_name: Berge's theorem and the Tutte–Berge formula
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Berge's augmenting path theorem (a matching is maximum if and only if there is no augmenting path) and of the Tutte–Berge formula (the maximum size of a matching is the minimum over vertex sets U of (|V| + |U| − odd(G − U)) / 2), with the weak inequality for all matchings and vertex sets; the formula is derived from Mathlib's Tutte theorem by adding universal vertices.

records.name: KKP.connected_counterexample_family
records.entry_name: Connected counterexamples to the exact color-critical two-eigenvalue bound
records.doc: For F=K5 minus one edge, a color-critical graph of chromatic number four, the graph formed from K(s,s,s) and K4 by one bridge is connected and F-free for every integer s at least three. It has 3s squared plus 7 edges, and the sum of squares of its two largest ordered adjacency eigenvalues exceeds 4m/3 by at least (656s squared-1366s+62)/(3(37s-1) squared)>0. The family has arbitrarily large edge counts, refuting the exact assertion in KKP Conjecture 1.16 and Li–Liu–Zhang Conjecture 5.4.

records.name: Glennie.SubmissionR03.q26_eq_iff_fullLedger_eq
records.entry_name: Finite Observations and Recognition of the Compact Albert Algebra
records.doc:
Let J=H_3(O), the real algebra of 3×3 Hermitian matrices over the division octonions, with product a∘b=(ab+ba)/2 and diagonal trace T. A frame p=(p_0,p_1,p_2) consists of trace-one elements satisfying p_i∘p_i=p_i, p_i∘p_j=0 for i≠j, and p_0+p_1+p_2=1. For frames p,q,r, record the 27 pair traces T(p_i∘q_j), T(q_j∘r_k), T(r_k∘p_i), and 27 triple traces T((p_i∘q_j)∘r_k), for i,j,k∈{0,1,2}. How much do these traces determine?

Each trace list in some open neighborhood of the data with pair entries 1/3 and triple entries 1/9, in a fixed twenty-dimensional chart, determines exactly two equivalence classes. Equivalence means one product-and-trace-preserving real linear bijection acting on all nine labeled elements, without relabeling. The sign of the degree-nine scalar Phi distinguishes the classes. With x=p_2−p_0, y=q_2−q_0, z=r_2−r_0, define

B(a,b) = T(a∘b),
U_a(b) = 2a∘(a∘b)−(a∘a)∘b,
Phi(x,y,z) = B((U_x U_y−U_y U_x)z,U_z(x∘y)).

Phi's derivative uses Glennie's degree-eight vector polynomial.

For arbitrary x,y,z∈J, Phi≠0 implies that 1,x,y,z generate J.

Recognition starts from a homogeneous cubic N on finite-dimensional real normed E, with N(e)=1 and g_e=−(1/3)D²(log N)_e positive definite on all E. A supplied linear equivalence ker(DN_e)≃ker T (the trace-zero subspace), matching g_e to B/3 and full vector-valued curvature tensors, yields an Albert algebra equivalence.

Consider 27 fixed parenthesized products of a distinguished element and three chosen elements in a real inner-product space with bilinear multiplication. Exact matching with the Albert table of pairwise inner products, inner products of products with these expressions and full ambient squared product norms determines a unique isometric, product-preserving linear embedding of J onto the subspace they generate under products and linear combinations, preserving the distinguished element and chosen elements.

A frame p=(p_0,p_1,p_2) consists of trace-one elements satisfying p_i∘p_i=p_i, p_i∘p_j=0 for i≠j, and p_0+p_1+p_2=1. For frames p,q,r, record the 27 pair traces T(p_i∘q_j), T(q_j∘r_k), T(r_k∘p_i), and 27 triple traces T((p_i∘q_j)∘r_k), for i,j,k∈{0,1,2}. How much do these traces determine?

Each trace list in some open neighborhood of the data with pair entries 1/3 and triple entries 1/9, in a fixed twenty-dimensional chart, determines exactly two equivalence classes. Equivalence means one product-and-trace-preserving real linear bijection acting on all nine labeled elements, without relabeling. The sign of the degree-nine scalar Phi distinguishes the classes. With x=p_2−p_0, y=q_2−q_0, z=r_2−r_0, define

B(a,b) = T(a∘b),
U_a(b) = 2a∘(a∘b)−(a∘a)∘b,
Phi(x,y,z) = B((U_x U_y−U_y U_x)z,U_z(x∘y)).

Phi's derivative uses Glennie's degree-eight vector polynomial.

For arbitrary x,y,z∈J, Phi≠0 implies that 1,x,y,z generate J.

Recognition starts from a homogeneous cubic N on finite-dimensional real normed E, with N(e)=1 and g_e=−(1/3)D²(log N)_e positive definite on all E. A supplied linear equivalence ker(DN_e)≃ker T (the trace-zero subspace), matching g_e to B/3 and full vector-valued curvature tensors, yields an Albert algebra equivalence.

Consider 27 fixed parenthesized products of a distinguished element and three chosen elements in a real inner-product space with bilinear multiplication. Exact matching with the Albert table of pairwise inner products, inner products of products with these expressions and full ambient squared product norms determines a unique isometric, product-preserving linear embedding of J onto the subspace they generate under products and linear combinations, preserving the distinguished element and chosen elements.

Further results give error bounds. All project exposition and Lean code are AI-generated under Robert MacGregor's direction. Robert is a non-mathematician and welcomes mathematical collaboration: macgregor@gmail.com. No novelty is asserted.
